purpose: Pegfilgrastim-cbqv is used to lower your risk of getting serious infections when you are receiving certain chemotherapy treatments for cancer. Chemotherapy can reduce your white blood cells, which are the cells your body uses to fight infections. This medicine helps your body make more of those important infection-fighting cells.
how_it_works: Your bone marrow is like a factory that makes blood cells. This medicine works by signaling your bone marrow to produce more white blood cells, specifically a type called neutrophils. More neutrophils in your blood means your body is better protected against dangerous infections during cancer treatment.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bone pain or aching, especially in your back, hips, or legs. You may also feel tired, have headaches, or notice some redness or soreness at the injection site. These side effects are usually manageable and temporary.
warnings: Call your doctor right away if you have severe pain in your upper left belly or left shoulder, as this could be a sign of a rare but serious spleen problem. Watch for signs of a severe allergic reaction like hives, trouble breathing, or swelling of the face. Do not use this medicine within 14 days before or 24 hours after receiving chemotherapy. Rarely, it can cause serious lung problems, so tell your doctor if you have new shortness of breath or fever.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as a single injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once per chemotherapy cycle. It is usually given the day after chemotherapy is finished. Your doctor or nurse will give you this injection, or you may be able to use a special on-body injector device that automatically delivers it about 27 hours after it is placed on your skin.
